_: AUTHORED BY HAND. What each surface IS, who it serves, and what reaches it. No walk can know these. probes/probe-surfaces.mjs merges this with a repo walk to write SURFACES.json.
_law: A SURFACE IS A USER INTERFACE POINT — somewhere a person acts on the system and it responds. Not a file, not a page, not a route. hall.html is a page; the Ask box is the surface. See SPEC-SURFACES.md.
_howToEdit: Add an entry when an interaction point acquires meaning. Never edit SURFACES.json — it is generated. If the walk reports UNDECLARED, that is a surface waiting for a sentence, not an error.
_theFourQuestions: `reaches` exists because these four were asked six times in one day on 27 Aug 2026 and could not be answered once: is it counted, does memory reach it, does the dial fire there, does it cost voice. A page-level register could answer none of them.
_honesty: Where a value is not known it is written as null, NOT as false. False is a claim; null is an admission. A register that guesses is worse than one that says it does not know.
_walkNote: The walk finds named interaction points by attribute — an id on an input, button or textarea. Its SECTION attribution is approximate: it reports the nearest preceding data-page, so a control inside a modal is filed under whichever section the modal happens to sit after in the source. Trust the authored `where.section` over the walked one.

walk.find: named interaction points: id on input|textarea|button, plus data-page sections and nav anchors
the panes. Their nav comes from fleet-nav.js, which is the pane registry and should be read as one.
the gameroom. Linked from Page1's nav as GAMEROOM and in no surface map until now.
the briefs as a stranger reads them. Reader surfaces with no interaction beyond links.

_notWalked: Admin and Amenti-Workers are private and cannot be walked from a runner without a token. Operator surfaces live in exactly those repos, which is why the probe belongs in Actions and not in a browser: a browser-side walk could map only half the subject and would report that half as the whole.

hall-ask.name: Ask Amenti
hall-ask.note: The hall's ONE interaction; everything else on that page is a link. Answers from HALL.md and HALL-STATE.json, citing documents by name. Neither hall.html nor this surface was in any register until 27 Aug 2026.

hall-search.name: the hall's fragment search
hall-search.note: THE SAME BOX as hall-ask. isQuestion() decides which of the two a keystroke becomes — a question goes to the model, a fragment searches the catalogue for nothing. One element, two surfaces, and the routing between them was the 26 Aug 'whom made amenti' bug.

terminal-input.name: the terminal
terminal-input.note: THE ONLY SURFACE THAT REACHES ALL FOUR, and the reason BRIEF-WHAT-AN-HOUR-COSTS prices one surface and calls it the product. Every instrument built on 26–27 Aug hangs off tune(), which serves this and nothing else.

terminal-mic.name: the terminal's microphone
terminal-mic.note: Push-to-talk. Costs Gemini on BOTH legs — STT in, TTS out — and /listen was metered on no axis at all until 28 Aug.

terminal-mode.name: the mode toggle
terminal-mode.note: Switches character/counsel. Costs nothing itself and changes which prompt the next turn uses.

counsel-input.name: Personal Counsel
counsel-input.note: A FULL CONVERSATION SURFACE THAT NO INSTRUMENT WATCHES. The visit reading fires from tune(), which counsel does not go through; AmentiMemory.load is never called here. Not a decision — an omission, and the first one the register was built to make visible. `dial` is null because whether the speaker toggle reaches this path has not been checked.

counsel-speak-all.name: read the counsel aloud
counsel-speak-all.note: NEVER HITS THE ARCHIVE. amenti-voice.js is explicit: the counsel's text is unique every turn, so every render is a fresh charge. The R2 archive serves the RECITAL path, not this one.

codex-search.name: the codex search
codex-search.note: Local filter over AMENTI_CHARS. No model call, no cost.

browse-search.name: the browse search
browse-search.note: Local. The walk files this under `timeline` because it reports the nearest preceding data-page; the authored section is right and the walked one is not.

talk-to-figure.name: TALK TO — the door to a soul
talk-to-figure.note: Not a conversation itself — it TUNES the terminal, and tune() is where the visit reading, the memory load and the memory writer all fire. The most load-bearing button in the application. Its drawer twin at Page1:5861 bypassed the click-map and 404'd until Codex.html was built on 26 Aug.

speaker-toggle.name: the speaker
speaker-toggle.note: THE ONLY SURFACE THE DIAL FIRES ON. Opening the line places a call — announcement, tone, ring — and the ring stops on the figure's first word. It covers a MEASURED silence: probe20 found render_ms = 7510 + 18.25 x chars, so a 110-char opener takes 9.5s to come back.

newsletter-signup.name: the newsletter signup
newsletter-signup.note: The only surface that WRITES to the vault directly from the browser. The anon key can insert a signup and execute an unsubscribe and nothing else — RLS on 25 of 25 tables.

quiz-answers.name: the quiz
quiz-answers.note: Scored server-side; the answers never reach the browser. TWO ELEMENTS CARRY id=quiz-close — STANDING SLIP #3, found by hand weeks ago and re-found by the first test run of the walk that does not exist yet.

page2.name: The Sovereign Instrument
page2.note: A SECOND APPLICATION with its own microphone, its own chunker (MAX_CHARS 1100, cited in the proxy's cost caps) and its own daily generation path. Named in FLEET_MANIFEST as a ship and ABSENT from SOURCES.json entirely until 27 Aug. Its own interaction points have not been enumerated — this entry is a placeholder for a page, which is precisely what §1 of the spec says a surface is not.

gameroom.name: the gameroom
gameroom.note: A WHOLE SURFACE IN A SEVENTH REPOSITORY. SOURCES.json has described it for weeks — 'linked from Page1's nav as GAMEROOM' — and nothing that maps surfaces could see it. Its interaction points are not enumerated. Its Pages site is unconfirmed, which is why doors.html leaves it named but unlinked.

qr-handover.name: the hand-over code
qr-handover.note: THE ONLY INTERACTION POINT THAT BEGINS OFF THE SYSTEM — a person points a camera and arrives, and no code walk can ever find it. It encodes location.href AT DRAW TIME, so it hands over whichever tab, figure or reading room the reader is on; there is no fixed printed URL. Tagged ?via=qr on 28 Aug, while nothing was printed, so a scan is countable from the first one.

doors.name: THE DOORS
doors.note: The seventeenth pane, built 26 Aug: one anchor per reachable document in SOURCES.json. Built with a reader half in mind, which is why it whitelists only repos whose Pages sites were confirmed — for an OPERATOR surface that is the wrong rule, since the captain wants to know a thing exists whether or not it serves.

spend.name: the spend reading
spend.note: NOT A SURFACE YET — a route with no interface on it. Recorded here so that when the Ledger pane is built it has something to point at, and so the register shows what is measured but not yet SHOWN. A route a person reads as raw JSON is an instrument without a face.

surface-manifest.name: The Surface Manifest
surface-manifest.note: The eighteenth pane, and the one that renders this register. IT APPEARS IN ITS OWN MAP DELIBERATELY — a map that omits itself is exactly the fault it was built to catch. Reads SURFACES.json; holds no list of its own.

gw-doorway.name: The Gateway Doorway
gw-doorway.note: THE FIRST THING ANYBODY TOUCHES. The gateway animation's own door — it opens the Interface and is, for most arrivals, the only control they meet before the site begins. Costs nothing and reaches nothing; its whole job is to be pressed once.

hero-cta-quiz.name: Start a Quiz
hero-cta-quiz.note: The arena's primary call to action. Opens the quiz surface, which mints against the emerald ledger — so it spends on the MINT rather than on Anthropic. One of the two doors the hero offers a stranger.

hero-cta-library.name: Browse the Library
hero-cta-library.note: The hero's second door, and the quieter one: it goes to the reading rooms rather than the economy. The pair is the whole of what the arena asks a stranger to choose between.

mp-play.name: Play / Pause
mp-play.note: The transport for ALREADY-RENDERED audio — it plays what the archive holds and renders nothing. costs is empty for that reason: the bill was paid when the clip was made. voice:true because it is an audio surface, not because it spends.

mp-prev.name: Previous
mp-prev.note: Steps back one track in the player's queue. Chrome around mp-play.

mp-next.name: Next
mp-next.note: Steps forward one track. Chrome around mp-play.

mp-close.name: Close the player
mp-close.note: Dismisses the player bar. It STOPS playback as well as hiding it — a player that keeps speaking from behind a closed panel is the forgotten tab in another costume.

councilBtn.name: Convene the Counsel
councilBtn.note: THE DOOR BETWEEN THE TWO CONVERSATION SURFACES. It sits on the terminal and opens the counsel chamber — the one control that carries a reader from talking to ONE figure to convening THREE. Costs nothing itself; what it opens does.

cnsBack.name: Back to the benches
cnsBack.note: Returns from a convened bench to the council tiles. Navigation only.

cnsFilter.name: Filter the bench
cnsFilter.note: Narrows the figure picker by name. Hidden until a bench is open. It is an INPUT that holds no conversation — the register's own reminder that kind:input does not imply a model call.

cnsAuto.name: Auto-pick
cnsAuto.note: Lets the council choose its own three, so a reader who does not know the roster is not stopped by it. The gentlest door into the chamber, and the one that most needs the `speaks` tags BUILD-THE-WAY-IN describes — without them it can only offer the obvious.

cnsGo.name: CONVENE
cnsGo.note: THE MOST EXPENSIVE PRESS IN THE PRODUCT. One convene is FOUR model calls — three figures answering in parallel, then a synthesis — and every one is unique text, so none of it caches. It does NOT use Amenti.chat: the chamber has its own counselSys(), a second counsel prompt that the chat core knows nothing about. Not counted by the visit reading.

quiz-close.name: Close the quiz
quiz-close.note: ⚠ DECLARED TWICE IN Page1.html — slip #3, found by hand weeks before the walk re-found it in its first minute. The second binding is unreachable, because getElementById returns the first. Fixing the page is a ten-minute job; the register keeps flagging it until somebody does.

quiz-shop.name: Claim and shop
quiz-shop.note: The reward path off a passed quiz — claims the emeralds and opens the shop. Its label is BUILT FROM THE RESULT, so the walk sees a template rather than text.

quiz-listen.name: Listen to the reading
quiz-listen.note: Reads the quiz passage aloud. RECITAL register, so it hits the R2 archive — fixed text, fixed boundaries, and a passage anybody has heard before is free. The opposite economics to cnsGo, on the same page.

quiz-retry.name: Try again / Next legend
quiz-retry.note: One button with two meanings, chosen by whether the quiz was passed. Costs nothing; the mint decides whether a retry can pay again.

dp-reader-close.name: Close the dispatch reader
dp-reader-close.note: Dismisses the day's dispatch reader. Navigation only — the dispatch is already rendered when it opens.

_stillUnknown: Page2's own interaction points. It is entered here as a page, which the spec says a surface is not — a placeholder until somebody walks it.
The gameroom's interaction points, for the same reason.
The seventeen panes. Each is an operator surface and none is entered; fleet-nav.js is their registry and should be read rather than retyped.
The reading vaults. Per-figure, generated, and their chat box is a conversation surface nobody has counted.
Whether the dial fires on counsel. Written as null rather than false, because nobody has checked.
